title: Maximum Good People Based on Statements
summary: Define two types of individuals: good people always tell the truth, while bad people may lie or tell the truth.
statement: Define two types of individuals: good people always tell the truth, while bad people may lie or tell the truth. Given a 0-indexed 2D integer array of size n x n representing statements made by n people about each other, where 0 means person i claims person j is bad, 1 means person i claims person j is good, and 2 means no statement, return the maximum number of people who can be good based on these statements.
constraints: Statements use zero for bad, one for good, and two for unknown; diagonal entries may be ignored.
Every person assumed good must have all definite statements agree with the assignment; bad people impose no constraint.
Return the greatest possible number of good people.
hints: The small n permits checking every proposed set of good people.
Encode an assignment as a bit mask; inspect only rows whose person bit is one.
Reject when any claim below two differs from the corresponding assignment bit; maximize valid bit counts.
Good rows are enforced exactly, bad rows remain unrestricted, and exhaustive masks include every possible classification.
editorial: Good rows are enforced exactly, bad rows remain unrestricted, and exhaustive masks include every possible classification.

tests.explanation: People zero and one can both be good consistently, giving maximum two.
Either person may be good alone, but both good contradict their statements, so the maximum is one.
